metadata.title: Adaptive Bound Optimization for Online Convex Optimization

nodes.name: Regret in online convex optimization
nodes.statement: $\Regret \equiv \sum_{t=1}^T f_t(x_t) - \min_{x \in \Fs} \sum_{t=1}^T f_t(x)$, where $\Fs \subseteq \reals^n$ is a closed bounded convex feasible set and $f_t$ are convex loss functions revealed online.

nodes.name: $\kappa$-competitive adaptive scheme
nodes.statement: An adaptive scheme is $\kappa$-competitive for the bound optimization problem if $B_R(\theta_1,\dots,\theta_T;f_1,\dots,f_T) \leq \kappa \inf_{\theta_1',\dots,\theta_T'} B_R(\theta_1',\dots,\theta_T';f_1,\dots,f_T)$ for all sequences $f_1,\dots,f_T$.

nodes.name: Proximal regularizer $r_t$
nodes.statement: $r_t(x) = \frac{1}{2}\|Q_t^{1/2}(x - x_t)\|_2^2$, where $Q_t \in \Snp$ is a positive semidefinite matrix centering the regularization at the current feasible point $x_t$.

nodes.name: Symmetric difference set $\Fsym$
nodes.statement: $\Fsym = \{x - x' \mid x, x' \in \Fs\}$ for a convex set $\Fs$.

nodes.name: Regret bound function $B_R$
nodes.statement: $B_R(\vec{Q_T}, \vec{g_T}) \equiv \frac{1}{2}\sum_{t=1}^T \max_{\hat{y} \in \Fsym}(\hat{y}^\top Q_t \hat{y}) + \sum_{t=1}^T g_t^\top Q_{1:t}^{-1} g_t$, where $g_t \in \partial f_t(x_t)$ and $Q_{1:t} = \sum_{\tau=1}^t Q_\tau$.

nodes.name: Matrix classes $\constQ, \diagQ, \fullQ$
nodes.statement: $\constQ = \{\alpha I \mid \alpha \geq 0\}$ (coordinate-constant); $\diagQ = \{\diag(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n) \mid \lambda_i \geq 0\}$ (diagonal); $\fullQ = \Snp$ (full PSD).

nodes.name: Lazy projection operator $\Proj_{\Fs,A}$
nodes.statement: $\Proj_{\Fs,A}(u) = \argmin_{x \in \Fs} \|A(x - u)\|$ projects an unconstrained point $u$ onto the feasible set $\Fs$ under the norm induced by $A$.

nodes.name: Coordinate width $D_i$
nodes.statement: $D_i = \max_{x, x' \in \Fs} |x_i - x'_i|$ is the width of $\Fs$ along the $i$th coordinate; the $D_i$ implicitly define a hyperrectangle containing $\Fs$.

nodes.name: Bound optimization problem
nodes.statement: $\inf_{\vec{Q_T} \in \Qfs^T} B_R(\vec{Q_T}, \vec{g_T})$: choose the sequence of regularization matrices from a class $\Qfs \subseteq \Snp$ that minimizes the post-hoc regret bound.

nodes.name: FTPRL update
nodes.statement: $x_{t+1} = \argmin_{x \in \Fs} \left(\sum_{\tau=1}^t (r_\tau(x) + f_\tau(x))\right)$: select the next play by minimizing accumulated loss plus accumulated proximal regularization.

nodes.name: Linear-quadratic FTPRL update
nodes.statement: $x_{t+1} = \argmin_{x \in \Fs} \left(\frac{1}{2}\sum_{\tau=1}^t (x - x_\tau)^\top Q_\tau (x - x_\tau) + g_{1:t} \cdot x\right)$, the FTPRL update after the WLOG reduction to linear loss functions.

nodes.name: Closed-form unconstrained optimum
nodes.statement: $u_{t+1} = Q_{1:t}^{-1}\left(\sum_{\tau=1}^t Q_\tau x_\tau - g_{1:t}\right)$, the unconstrained minimizer that, after projection by $\Proj_{\Fs,A_t}$, gives $x_{t+1}$.

nodes.name: Bad family for non-adaptive regularization
nodes.statement: There exists a family of online convex optimization problems where subgradient descent with non-increasing learning rate (and FTPRL with non-decreasing coordinate-constant regularization) incurs regret $\Omega(T^{2/3})$, while FTPRL with appropriate diagonal $Q_t$ has regret $O(\sqrt{T})$.
assumptions: Online convex optimization setting parametrized by number of rounds $T$
conclusions: Subgradient descent with non-increasing learning rate suffers $\Omega(T^{2/3})$ regret
Any algorithm with $O(MD\sqrt{T})$ regret bound suffers $\Omega(T^{2/3})$ on this family

nodes.name: FTPRL adaptive-norms regret bound
nodes.statement: For closed bounded convex $\Fs$ with $0 \in \Fs$, $Q_1 \in \Snpp$, $Q_2,\dots,Q_T \in \Snp$, FTPRL with $r_t(x) = \frac{1}{2}\|Q_t^{1/2}(x-x_t)\|^2$ satisfies $\Regret \leq r_{1:T}(\mathring{x}) + \sum_{t=1}^T \|A_t^{-1} g_t\|^2$ with $A_t = Q_{1:t}^{1/2}$ and $\mathring{x} = \argmin_{x \in \Fs} f_{1:T}(x)$.

nodes.name: Arbitrary feasible set competitive ratio
nodes.statement: Let $\Fs$ be an arbitrary feasible set with $H^{\text{in}} \subseteq \Fs \subseteq H^{\text{out}}$ for hyperrectangles of widths $w_i, W_i$, and $\beta = \max_i W_i / w_i$. Then FTPRL-Diag is $\sqrt{2}\beta$-competitive with $\diagQ$ on $\Fs$.
assumptions: $H^{\text{in}} \subseteq \Fs \subseteq H^{\text{out}}$ with hyperrectangles of widths $w_i > 0$ and $W_i$

nodes.name: Optimal diagonal $Q$ on $L_p$ balls
nodes.section: 3.3 Post-hoc bound for diagonal regularization on $L_p$ balls
nodes.statement: For $p > 2$, the optimal regularization matrix for $B_R$ in $\diagQ$ is not coordinate-constant (not in $\constQ$), except in the degenerate case where $G_i = \sum_{t=1}^T g_{t,i}^2$ is the same for all $i$. For $p \leq 2$, the optimal regularization matrix in $\diagQ$ always belongs to $\constQ$.
assumptions: Bound function $B_R$ from Eq. \eqref{eq:fixedQF} restricted to $\diagQ$

nodes.name: Black-box transformation to unit norm ball
nodes.section: 3.4 Full matrix regularization on hyperspheres and hyperellipsoids
nodes.statement: For instance $\inst = (\Fs,(g_1,\dots,g_T))$ with $\Fs = \{x \mid \|Ax\| \leq 1\}$, $A \in \Snpp$, define $\hinst = (\hFs, (\hat{g}_1,\dots,\hat{g}_T))$ with $\hFs = \{\hat{x} \mid \|\hat{x}\| \leq 1\}$ and $\hat{g}_t = A^{-1} g_t$. Then any subgradient-only algorithm on $\hinst$ playing $\hat{x}_t$ achieves identical loss/regret on $\inst$ via $x_t = A^{-1}\hat{x}_t$, and the post-hoc optimal bound over $Q \in \Snpp$ is identical for both instances.
conclusions: Identical loss/regret achieved by playing $x_t = A^{-1}\hat{x}_t$ on $\inst$ corresponding to $\hat{x}_t$ on $\hinst$
Post-hoc optimal bound over $Q \in \Snpp$ is identical for $\inst$ and $\hinst$

nodes.name: FTPRL-Scale competitive on hyperellipsoids
nodes.section: 3.4 Full matrix regularization on hyperspheres and hyperellipsoids
nodes.statement: The diagonal-constant algorithm (Cor. \ref{cor:global}) is $\sqrt{2}$-competitive with $\Snp$ when $\Fs = \{x \mid \|x\|_p \leq 1\}$ for $p=2$, and $\sqrt{2}$-competitive with $\diagQ$ for $p \in [1,2)$. FTPRL-Scale extends these guarantees to $\Fs = \{x \mid \|Ax\|_p \leq 1\}$ for $A \in \Snpp$.
conclusions: Coordinate-constant algorithm is $\sqrt{2}$-competitive with $\Snp$ on $L_2$ ball
FTPRL-Scale achieves the same competitive guarantees on hyperellipsoids
$\Regret \leq \sqrt{2} \inf_{Q \in \Snp} (\max_{y \in \Fs}(2y^\top Qy) + \sum_{t=1}^T g_t^\top Q^{-1} g_t)$ when $\Fs$ is the unit $L_2$ ball

nodes.name: FTRL regret decomposition
nodes.statement: For non-negative functions $r_1,\dots,r_T$, the regret of FTPRL satisfies $\Regret \leq r_{1:T}(\mathring{x}) + \sum_{t=1}^T (f_t(x_t) - f_t(x_{t+1}))$, where $\mathring{x}$ is the post-hoc optimal feasible point.
assumptions: FTPRL plays $x_t$ as defined by Eq. \eqref{eq:ftrlx}

nodes.name: Lazy-projection equivalence
nodes.statement: Let $Q \in \Snpp$, $h \in \R^n$, $f(x) = h^\top x + \frac{1}{2}x^\top Q x$, $\mathring{u} = \argmin_{u} f(u)$, $A = Q^{1/2}$. Then $\Proj_{\Fs,A}(\mathring{u}) = \argmin_{x \in \Fs} f(x)$.

nodes.name: Projection contractivity
nodes.statement: Let $Q \in \Snpp$, $A = Q^{1/2}$, $\Fs$ convex, $u_1, u_2 \in \R^n$, $x_i = \Proj_{\Fs,A}(u_i)$. Then $\|A(x_2 - x_1)\| \leq \|A(u_1 - u_2)\|$.

nodes.name: Per-round regret bound via dual norms
Auer-style sum bound
nodes.section: 3 Specific Adaptive Algorithms and Competitive Ratios
nodes.statement: For any non-negative reals $x_1,\dots,x_n$, $\sum_{i=1}^n \frac{x_i}{\sqrt{\sum_{j=1}^i x_j}} \leq 2 \sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i}$.

nodes.name: Be-the-leader has non-positive regret
nodes.statement: For any sequence of functions $f_1,\dots,f_T$ and any $\Fs$, with $x^*_t = \argmin_{x \in \Fs} \sum_{\tau=1}^t f_\tau(x)$, we have $\sum_{t=1}^T f_t(x^*_t) \leq \sum_{t=1}^T f_t(x^*_T)$.

nodes.name: BTRL regret bound
nodes.statement: For non-negative functions $r_1,\dots,r_T$, BTRL (which plays $\hat{x}_t = \argmin_{x \in \Fs}(r_{1:t}(x) + f_{1:t}(x))$) has regret at most $r_{1:T}(\mathring{x})$, where $\mathring{x}$ is the post-hoc optimal solution.

nodes.name: Coordinate-constant FTPRL bound
nodes.statement: If FTPRL uses diagonal matrices with $(Q_{1:t})_{ii} = \bar{\alpha}_t = 2\sqrt{G_t}/D$ where $G_t = \sum_{\tau=1}^t \sum_{i=1}^n g_{\tau,i}^2$ and $D$ is the $L_2$-diameter of $\Fs$, then $\Regret \leq 2D\sqrt{G_T}$. When $\Fs = \{x \mid \|x\|_2 \leq D/2\}$, this is $\sqrt{2}$-competitive over $\constQ$.
conclusions: When $\Fs$ is the $L_2$-ball of radius $D/2$, the algorithm is $\sqrt{2}$-competitive over $\constQ$

nodes.name: Per-coordinate diagonal FTPRL bound
nodes.statement: With diagonal $Q_t$ such that $(Q_{1:t})_{ii} = \bar{\lambda}_{t,i} = (2/D_i)\sqrt{\sum_{\tau=1}^t g_{\tau,i}^2}$, FTPRL satisfies $\Regret \leq 2 \sum_{i=1}^n D_i \sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^T g_{t,i}^2}$. When $\Fs$ is a hyperrectangle, the algorithm is $\sqrt{2}$-competitive with the post-hoc optimum over $\diagQ$.
assumptions: Convex feasible set $\Fs$ with width $D_i$ in coordinate $i$

nodes.name: FTPRL-Diag
nodes.statement: Per-coordinate adaptive diagonal regularization for FTPRL on hyperrectangle-bounded feasible sets, computing $Q_t$ entries adaptively from squared gradient sums.
output: Sequence of plays $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_T$ with regret bounded as in Cor. \ref{cor:percoord}

nodes.name: FTPRL-Scale
nodes.section: 3.4 Full matrix regularization on hyperspheres and hyperellipsoids (Algorithm 2)
nodes.statement: Adaptive FTPRL for transformed-norm feasible sets $\Fs \subseteq \{x \mid \|Ax\| \leq 1\}$ that runs the coordinate-constant scheme on the unit norm ball after the change of variables $\hat{x} = Ax$.
output: Sequence of plays $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_T$ achieving $\sqrt{2}$-competitive regret

nodes.name: Heavy-tailed feature distribution
nodes.statement: $\Fs = [-1/2, 1/2]^n$, $g_{t,i} = 1$ w.p. $i^{-\alpha}$ for $\alpha \in [1,2)$, else $0$. Gradient descent with global learning rate gets $O(\sqrt{nT})$, while adaptive algorithms achieve $O(\sqrt{T} \cdot n^{1-\alpha/2})$ via Jensen's inequality.

nodes.name: Diagonal scaling $A = \diag(1/a_1,\ldots,1/a_n)$
nodes.section: 3.4 Full matrix regularization on hyperspheres and hyperellipsoids
nodes.statement: For $\Fs = \{x \mid \|Ax\|_2 \leq 1\}$ with $A = \diag(1/a_1,\dots,1/a_n)$, $\max_i a_i = 1$: direct Cor. \ref{cor:global} gives $\Regret \leq 4\sqrt{\sum_i G_i}$, while FTPRL-Scale achieves $\Regret \leq 4\sqrt{\sum_i a_i^2 G_i}$, much better when $a_i \ll 1$.

nodes.name: Reduction to linear loss functions
nodes.statement: By convexity of $f_t$, $f_t(x) \geq g_t^\top(x - x_t) + f_t(x_t)$ with equality at $x_t$, so regret against affine surrogates upper-bounds true regret; the affine term can be replaced by the linear $g_t^\top x$. Thus WLOG the loss functions are linear when the algorithm uses only subgradients.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma \ref{lem:lazy_proj}
nodes.statement: Show $\argmin_{x \in \Fs} f(x) = \argmin_{x \in \Fs} f'(x) = \Proj_{\Fs,A}(\mathring{u})$ where $f'(x) = \frac{1}{2}\|Q^{1/2}(x - \mathring{u})\|^2$ differs from $f(x)$ only by a constant in $x$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma \ref{lem:a_proj}
nodes.statement: Use first-order optimality conditions for the projections, combine the two inequalities, and apply $Q$-symmetry to derive $\hat{u}^\top Q \hat{u} \geq \hat{x}^\top Q \hat{x}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem \ref{thm:adaptive_norms}
nodes.statement: Express $x_t, x_{t+1}$ as projections via Lemma \ref{lem:lazy_proj}, apply Lemma \ref{lem:not_btarl_term} to bound per-round difference $g_t^\top(x_t - x_{t+1}) \leq \|A_t^{-1}g_t\|^2$, then combine via Lemma \ref{lem:ftrl}.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary \ref{cor:global}
nodes.statement: Bound the LHS of $B_R$ by $D\sqrt{G_T}$ via $\hat{y}_t^\top \hat{y}_t \leq D^2$, bound the RHS by $D\sqrt{G_T}$ via Lemma \ref{lem:sum}; for the lower bound on the post-hoc optimum, solve the 1D minimization analytically when $\Fs$ is the $L_2$ ball.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary \ref{cor:percoord}
nodes.statement: Bound LHS and RHS of $B_R$ per-coordinate using $\hat{y}_{t,i}^2 \leq D_i^2$ and Lemma \ref{lem:sum}. For the hyperrectangle case, decompose Eq. \eqref{eq:fixedQ} per coordinate and minimize the resulting 1D problem in $\lambda_i$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem \ref{thm:arbcomp}
nodes.statement: Upper-bound FTPRL-Diag regret using outer hyperrectangle widths $W_i$ from Cor. \ref{cor:percoord}; lower-bound the post-hoc optimum on $\Fs$ by the post-hoc optimum on the inner hyperrectangle $H^{\text{in}}$ (which has widths $w_i \geq W_i/\beta$); take the ratio.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem \ref{thm:lp_posthoc}
nodes.section: 3.3 Post-hoc bound for diagonal regularization on $L_p$ balls
nodes.statement: For $p \geq 2$, change variables $z_i = y_i^2$, identify $\|z\|_{p/2} \leq 1$ and use dual-norm $\|\lambda\|_q$ with $q = p/(p-2)$; differentiate to show non-constant $\lambda$ is required when $G_i$ differ. For $p \in [1,2]$, show the LHS reduces to $2\|\lambda\|_\infty$, then any optimum has all $\lambda_i$ equal.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem \ref{thm:blackbox}
nodes.section: 3.4 Full matrix regularization on hyperspheres and hyperellipsoids
nodes.statement: Use change of variable $\hat{x} = Ax$: $\hat{g}_t^\top \hat{x}_t = g_t^\top x_t$ implies identical losses; minimization over $\{x: \|Ax\| \leq 1\}$ equals minimization over $\{\hat{x}: \|\hat{x}\| \leq 1\}$ after substitution. For the post-hoc bound, set $\hat{Q} = A^{-1} Q A^{-1}$ to map $\inst$ bounds to $\hinst$ bounds bijectively.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem \ref{thm:sphere}
nodes.section: 3.4 Full matrix regularization on hyperspheres and hyperellipsoids
nodes.statement: For $p=2$: factor $Q = PDP^\top$, show optimal $D = \alpha I$, solve 1D problem $B(\alpha) = 2\alpha + G_T/\alpha$, get $2\sqrt{2G_T}$ vs $4\sqrt{G_T}$ achieved by Cor. \ref{cor:global}, ratio $\sqrt{2}$. For $p \in [1,2)$, combine Theorems \ref{thm:lp_posthoc} and \ref{thm:blackbox}.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma \ref{lem:btl}
nodes.statement: Induction on $T$: trivial for $T=1$; for the inductive step, use the IH on $\sum_{t=1}^{T-1} f_t(x^*_t) \leq \sum_{t=1}^{T-1} f_t(x^*_{T-1})$, then replace $x^*_{T-1}$ by $x^*_T$ using the definition of $x^*_{T-1}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma \ref{lem:btrl}
nodes.statement: Define $f'_t(x) = f_t(x) + r_t(x)$, observe $\hat{x}_t = \argmin_x f'_{1:t}(x)$, apply Lemma \ref{lem:btl} to the $f'_t$, then drop the non-negative $r_t(\hat{x}_t)$ terms.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma \ref{lem:ftrl}
nodes.statement: Combine Lemma \ref{lem:btrl} with the observation that FTRL loss exceeds BTRL loss by $\sum_{t=1}^T (f_t(x_t) - f_t(\hat{x}_t))$ where $\hat{x}_t = x_{t+1}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma \ref{lem:sum}
nodes.statement: Induction on $n$: base case trivial; for step, write $\sum \leq 2\sqrt{Z - x_n} + x_n/\sqrt{Z}$, take derivative in $x_n$ to show RHS is decreasing in $x_n \geq 0$, so maximum at $x_n = 0$ gives $2\sqrt{Z}$.

nodes.name: Reduce to per-round bound
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{lem:ftrl}, it suffices to show $f_t(x_t) - f_t(x_{t+1}) \leq \|A_t^{-1} g_t\|^2$ for all $t$ (Eq. \eqref{eq:toprove}).

nodes.name: Express $x_t, x_{t+1}$ as projections
nodes.statement: Use $x_t = \argmin_{x \in \Fs} r_t(x)$ and Eq. \eqref{eq:rtt} to write $x_t = \argmin (h^\top x + \frac{1}{2}x^\top Q_{1:t} x)$ with $h = g_{1:t-1} - q_{1:t}$; similarly $x_{t+1}$ uses $h + g_t$.

nodes.name: Apply lazy-projection lemma
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{lem:lazy_proj}, $x_t = \Proj_{\Fs,A_t}(-Q_{1:t}^{-1} h)$ and $x_{t+1} = \Proj_{\Fs,A_t}(-Q_{1:t}^{-1}(h + g_t))$.

nodes.name: Bound per-round difference
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{lem:not_btarl_term}, $g_t^\top (x_t - x_{t+1}) \leq \|A_t^{-1} g_t\|^2$, which yields Eq. \eqref{eq:toprove} (using linearity).

nodes.name: Conclude via Lemma \ref{lem:ftrl}
nodes.statement: Combine the per-round bound with Lemma \ref{lem:ftrl} to obtain $\Regret \leq r_{1:T}(\mathring{x}) + \sum_t \|A_t^{-1} g_t\|^2$.

nodes.name: Bound LHS of $B_R$
nodes.statement: $\frac{1}{2}\sum_t \hat{y}_t^\top Q_t \hat{y}_t \leq \frac{1}{2} D^2 \sum_t \alpha_t = \frac{1}{2} D^2 \bar{\alpha}_T = D\sqrt{G_T}$ using $\hat{y}_t^\top \hat{y}_t \leq D^2$.

nodes.name: Bound RHS via Lemma \ref{lem:sum}
nodes.statement: $\sum_t g_t^\top Q_{1:t}^{-1} g_t = \frac{D}{2} \sum_t \frac{\sum_i g_{t,i}^2}{\sqrt{G_t}} \leq D\sqrt{G_T}$ by Lemma \ref{lem:sum}.

nodes.name: Lower bound the post-hoc optimum on the $L_2$ ball
nodes.statement: When $\Fs$ is the $L_2$ ball of radius $D/2$, Eq. \eqref{eq:fixedQ} simplifies to $\min_{\alpha \geq 0} (\frac{1}{2}\alpha D^2 + G_T/\alpha) = D\sqrt{2 G_T}$; ratio $\sqrt{2}$ proves competitiveness.

nodes.name: Per-coordinate LHS bound
nodes.statement: $\frac{1}{2}\sum_t \hat{y}_t^\top Q_t \hat{y}_t \leq \frac{1}{2}\sum_i D_i^2 \bar{\lambda}_{T,i} = \sum_i D_i \sqrt{\sum_t g_{t,i}^2}$ using $\hat{y}_{t,i}^2 \leq D_i^2$.

nodes.name: Per-coordinate RHS bound
nodes.statement: $\sum_t g_t^\top Q_{1:t}^{-1} g_t = \sum_i (D_i/2) \sum_t g_{t,i}^2/\sqrt{\sum_{\tau \leq t} g_{\tau,i}^2} \leq \sum_i D_i \sqrt{\sum_t g_{t,i}^2}$ via Lemma \ref{lem:sum}.

nodes.name: Decompose post-hoc problem on hyperrectangle
nodes.statement: When $\Fs$ is a hyperrectangle, Eq. \eqref{eq:fixedQ} decomposes per coordinate; choose $\hat{y}_i^2 = D_i^2$ and minimize $\frac{1}{2}\lambda_i D_i^2 + (1/\lambda_i)\sum_t g_{t,i}^2$ in $\lambda_i$ to get $\sqrt{2}\sum_i D_i\sqrt{\sum_t g_{t,i}^2}$, ratio $\sqrt{2}$.

nodes.name: Reduce to dual norm for $p \geq 2$
nodes.statement: Set $z_i = y_i^2$, identify $\sum_i z_i^{p/2} \leq 1 \Leftrightarrow \|z\|_{p/2} \leq 1$; reduces LHS maximization to $2\|\lambda\|_q$ with $q = p/(p-2)$.

nodes.name: Differentiate $B(\lambda)$ for $p > 2$
nodes.statement: $\nabla B(\lambda)_i = 2(\lambda_i/\|\lambda\|_q)^{q-1} - G_i/\lambda_i^2$; setting all $\lambda_i$ equal gives gradient $2 n^{1/q - 1} - G_i/\lambda_1^2$, non-zero when $G_i$ differ, so constant $\lambda$ cannot be optimal.

nodes.name: Reduce to $\|\lambda\|_\infty$ form for $p \in [1,2]$
nodes.statement: For $p = 2$ this follows from $q = \infty$; for $p \in [1,2)$, lower bound by setting $y$ = single coordinate, upper bound by inclusion in $L_2$ ball; conclude optimal $\lambda$ has all entries equal.

nodes.name: Diagonalize $Q$
nodes.statement: Write $Q = P D P^\top$ with $D = \diag(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)$ positive eigenvalues, $PP^\top = I$, $Q^{-1} = P D^{-1} P^\top$.

nodes.name: Reduce post-hoc bound to scalar problem
nodes.statement: On the unit $L_2$ ball, Eq. \eqref{eq:l_one_two_post} is tight: $2\max_i \lambda_i + \sum_t g_t^\top P D^{-1} P^\top g_t$. Optimum has $D = \alpha I$, giving $B(\alpha) = 2\alpha + G_T/\alpha$.

nodes.name: Compute competitive ratio
nodes.statement: Optimum at $\alpha = \sqrt{G_T/2}$ gives post-hoc bound $2\sqrt{2 G_T}$ vs Cor. \ref{cor:global} bound $4\sqrt{G_T}$ (using $D = 2$); ratio $\sqrt{2}$. For $p \in [1,2)$, combine Theorems \ref{thm:lp_posthoc} and \ref{thm:blackbox}.

nodes.name: Initialize
nodes.statement: $x_1 = 0 \in \Fs$; for all $i$, $G_i = 0$, $q_i = 0$, $\lambda_{0,i} = 0$, $D_i = b_i - a_i$.

nodes.name: Outer loop over rounds
nodes.statement: for $t = 1$ to $T$: play $x_t$, incur $f_t(x_t)$, get $g_t \in \partial f_t(x_t)$; perform per-coordinate update (inner loop) and projection.

nodes.name: Per-coordinate update
nodes.statement: for $i = 1$ to $n$: $G_i \mathrel{+}= g_{t,i}^2$; $\lambda_{t,i} = (2/D_i)\sqrt{G_i} - \lambda_{1:t-1,i}$; $q_i \mathrel{+}= x_{t,i}\lambda_{t,i}$; $u_{t+1,i} = (g_{1:t,i} - q_i)/\lambda_{1:t,i}$.

nodes.name: Project onto $\Fs$
nodes.statement: $A_t = \diag(\sqrt{\lambda_{1:t,1}}, \dots, \sqrt{\lambda_{1:t,n}})$; $x_{t+1} = \Proj_{\Fs, A_t}(u_{t+1})$.

nodes.name: Initialize
nodes.statement: $\hFs = \{x \mid \|x\| \leq 1\}$; $x_1 = 0$; for all $i$, $D_i = b_i - a_i$.

nodes.name: Outer loop over rounds
nodes.statement: for $t = 1$ to $T$: play $x_t$, incur $f_t(x_t)$, get $g_t \in \partial f_t(x_t)$; transform gradient $\hat{g}_t = (A^{-1})^\top g_t$.

nodes.name: Coordinate-constant adaptive update on $\hFs$
nodes.statement: $\bar{\alpha} = \sqrt{\sum_{\tau \leq t}\sum_i \hat{g}_{\tau,i}^2}$; $\alpha_t = \bar{\alpha} - \alpha_{1:t-1}$; $q_t = \alpha_t x_t$; $\hat{u}_{t+1} = (1/\bar{\alpha})(q_{1:t} - g_{1:t})$; $A_t = (\bar{\alpha} I)^{1/2}$.
